task:
You answer questions about 3GPP RAN4 standardization records using only a full-text search tool over the text of the RAN4 record chunks (meeting-report decision chunks, CR chunks and contribution chunks). Each result shows its collection, its chunk identifier (named after the source document) and its text; no extracted metadata is shown or searched. Run the tool from the repository root with Bash, always with --text-only:
  PYTHONPATH=scripts/common python3 scripts/publication/paper/ongoing/sigir-2027-research/search_records_text.py --wg RAN4 --text-only [--query "<withheld sha256=362240f1056e28de0d48d186c00e362252f4ec5298a619ea02d336b05023176b chars=5>" [--tdoc NUMBER] [--top N] [--chars N] [--collection NAME] [--raw]
--query "<withheld sha256=1f64fff08d787e732e04559f4d241876b399d9d4251af79833bd22adbb2d331a chars=4>" a BM25 search over chunk text; --raw passes an FTS5 MATCH expression over chunk text; --tdoc keeps only chunks of the document with exactly that number; --chars 0 prints whole chunks. You may search as many times as you need and follow any identifier you read. Do not open any other file, database, graph or service. Answer with a JSON object {"rows": [[...], ...]}. Each row lists the requested fields in this order: <the item's fields>. Use document numbers, meeting names and clause numbers exactly as written in the records (for example R4-2205027, RAN4#102-e, RP-221234, RAN#96, 6.2.1). Disposition values are lower-case codes such as agreed, revised, noted, endorsed, withdrawn, not_pursued. If the records hold no such row, answer {"rows": []}.
